source_facts: Every infer call first accepts a checked-cache entry regardless of flag.
Baseline InferOnly may then accept an infer_cache_no_check entry, while baseline Check cannot.
The mutation reverses that second selection: Check may accept infer_cache_no_check, while InferOnly no longer reads that cache.
Both versions still write InferOnly results to infer_cache_no_check and Check results to infer_cache_check.

On a cold first InferOnly call the changed read guard cannot affect the returned value because no no-check entry exists. A following Check call on the same expression isolates the consequential change: baseline recomputes with checks, while the mutant may return the weak cached value.

freshness_boundary: ExportFile::check_declar uses with_tc_and_declar for each axiom, definition, theorem, opaque, constructor, and recursor header. That helper constructs a new LeanDag, TcCtx, TypeChecker, and TcCache.

For a definition, theorem, or opaque, check_declar_info and infer(value, Check) share that one fresh checker, so within-declaration ordering is possible; cross-declaration or pretty-printer warming is not.

The ordinary value entry is Check and its app, lambda, pi, and let structural recursion propagates Check. There is no direct ordinary entry that intentionally performs InferOnly on the whole declaration value before Check.
proof_irrelevance_trace: def_eq first applies whnf_no_unfolding_cheap_proj to both operands and repeats its quick checks before proof_irrel_eq.
whnf_no_unfolding_aux reduces a head Let by substituting its value into its body.

proof_irrel_eq then calls is_proof, whose InferOnly operates on the normalized operands. Consequently, placing the malformed candidate Let directly as a proof-irrelevance operand does not warm the no-check cache for that original head-Let pointer.

The eta-structure, eta-expansion, and unit fallback InferOnly calls also receive the post-normalization operands. Nested expressions can still be traversed by InferOnly, so this observation is not a general unreachability proof.

reduction_trace.consequential_order: For a K recursor, to_ctor_when_k weakly infers the exact major expression before reduce_rec normalizes that major. If the major is the malformed Let E and the same interned expression pointer is structurally visited later in Check mode in the same declaration, this call graph has the required InferOnly(E) then Check(E) order.

Source does not itself supply a concrete export record satisfying the K-recursor environment, equality-reduction trigger, sequencing, and later repeated checked occurrence together.

Inductive checking contains additional InferOnly sites with explicit nearby cache clears and is a distinct specialized path.

ordinary_exported_declaration_reachabili.conclusion: Ordinary exported declaration checking is not proven immune: a concrete same-checker call path can weakly infer a recursor major before a later strong visit. This review does not establish that a realizable export artifact reaches the exact harmful ordering, and it does not establish that all ordinary exports avoid it. The smallest currently justified execution is the internal cache-contract comparison; export-level reachability remains an explicit follow-up question.
